newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Argentine ADRs slip on weak Dow.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Argentine ADRs slip on weak Dow.

text.p: Argentine shares were mostly weaker in thin U.S. trade Tuesday as profit-taking on Wall Street and a higher U.S. long bond yield weighed on Latin American stocks.
"It's just a slight pullback, basically because the Dow isn't making a 74-point gain like it did yesterday. I think it's purely interest-rate driven and Dow Jones-related," one trader said.
YPF's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) slid 1/8 to 22-1/2 by early afternoon after posting a two percent gain on Monday, while Telefnica slipped 1/8 to 24-1/2.
Banco de Galicia shed 1/4 to 22-1/4, and BAESA lost 1/8 to trade at 6-5/8 by early afternoon.
The Dow was off 21.46 points, or 0.37 percent, at 5712.38, while the benchmark U.S. long bond yield crept higher to 7.13 percent after closing at 7.07 percent Monday.
Mexican shares also drifted lower on weak volumes, with Telmex off 1/8 at 32-3/4, Televisa down 1/4 at 30-1/4, and Tribasa flat at 5-3/4.
Brazil's Telebras managed to inch up 1/8 to 76-1/2, and Chile's CTC firmed 1/8 to 98-1/4, both in slow trade.
Elsewhere, Britain's Danka continued higher on follow-through buying spurred by its pact to buy Eastman Kodak's copier distribution business, announced on Monday.
"The deal is perceived to be very good for them. This gets them involved in a bigger leg of the business," a trader said.
Danka's ADRs gained nearly two percent, rising 5/8 to 37-1/8 after soaring Monday.
In other activity, SmithKline Beecham fell one to 58-7/8 after Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock to neutral from outperform.
Gucci also fell, dropping 1-3/4 to 68-5/8, despite Smith Barney's initiating coverage with a buy rating.
"Gucci's had a big bounce recently. This could just be a little bit of consolidation," a trader said.
